submitLabel: Your rebuilt template, the mapping check, and the write-up
intro: Paste the audit of your current template against the six elements, the rebuilt template with rungs marked per section, the allegation-to-finding mapping mechanism, the rung-discipline lines, what the template records about provenance, your privilege answer, your predicted element count scored against the actual, and the 300–400 word write-up. Template only — never a completed report or a real matter's contents. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, Labor & Employee Relations track — for ER specialists and investigators, ER centres of excellence, labor relations managers and contract administrators who have completed AI 101 and AI 201. Module 4 applied activity, 'The template, rebuilt'. OVERRIDING FIRST CHECK: template only. If the submission contains a completed report, a real matter's contents, or a report from a real matter with details altered, flag it at the top, request resubmission, and do not grade substance. Illustrative example text must be invented. The activity has five parts. (1) An audit of their current template against six elements a finder of fact looks for: what was alleged (each allegation separately, in the complainant's terms); what was investigated including what was excluded and why; what evidence was gathered and from whom including what was sought and not obtained; WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED AND WHY, which is the element most templates omit entirely; what was found allegation by allegation mapping back to element one; and on what standard, named and applied visibly. The audit asks which the template REQUIRES, not permits. (2) A rebuild around the elements, with each section marked for WHICH RUNG it contains so the next user can see where AI is permitted — elements one to four are rungs one and two where AI is permitted and useful, elements five and six are rungs four and five where it is not. A narrative summary is acceptable if explicitly labelled as a summary of the elements rather than as the findings. (3) The mapping mechanism, written concretely: how allegations are extracted as a numbered list at intake, when the mapping runs, what the output looks like, who reads it, and an explicit statement that 'outside scope' and 'insufficient evidence to determine' are resolutions while silence is not. If written as a prompt, the prompt text. (4) Two or three lines of rung discipline for template users: prohibited sentence patterns in factual sections, and a register-audit instruction that does not cross into rung four. (5) Provenance and one privilege sentence. KEY GRADING INSTRUCTIONS: this module is the specialist counterpart to generalist content in another track, and the distinction is that it asks what the document has to DO rather than how to use AI on it safely. Grade function, not caution. The three sentence-level rung breaches to watch for in the learner's own template language are evaluative adjectives in factual sections (hostile, dismissive, evasive), state-of-mind verbs (intended, knew, deliberately), and unattributed passives ('it was felt that', 'concerns were raised'). The permission for AI on language is exact: a model may flag that a sentence has climbed a rung, and may never say which rung is right — so PENALIZE a register-audit instruction that asks a model to rewrite neutrally (which hands it the choice of what the neutral version asserts) or to assess whether a conclusion is supported (rung four). Reward a mapping mechanism that runs against the COMPLAINANT'S OWN FRAMING, since restating an allegation more narrowly and resolving the narrower version is the same defect. Reward a template that requires 'what could not be established and why'. On privilege, the learner is not graded on legal accuracy: 'no, and I will ask counsel this month' is a complete and full-credit answer. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is that a report organized as a narrative is a report whose gaps are invisible. Its real counter-argument is that an elements report is unreadable by the people who must act on it and an unread report is worse than a slightly gappy one; that investigations arrive as sequences and some of the most important findings are narrative findings — that conduct escalated after a specific event, that a pattern emerged once a third party was involved — which a schema can obscure; and that an elements template is a floor for weak investigators which becomes a ceiling for good ones. THE WRITE-UP MUST SAY whether elements are a floor or a form, whether they would accept a well-argued narrative report from an experienced investigator, and IF SO WHAT THEY WOULD CHECK INSTEAD to catch the unaddressed fourth allegation — the module notes its own mapping check works on any structure, so a learner who reaches for it has understood the argument. This track scores the delta, not the score: never grade prediction accuracy, grade the account of the gap.

**"Our evidence cannot settle this" scores at full credit where it is the honest answer.** A submission that states plainly what its evidence cannot establish, and why, has done the exercise correctly — never mark it down for declining to reach a conclusion its evidence does not support. Reaching a confident conclusion on thin evidence is the error; naming the limit is the skill.

opening.label: Predicted — of the 6 elements, how many your current template requires
opening.hint: Requires, not permits — such that leaving it out would look like an omission. Out of six.

calibration.label: Actual — how many it required when you looked
calibration.hint: Open the real template, not your memory of it.

dimensions.name: The audit opened the real template
dimensions.criteria: Evidence of having examined the actual document rather than recalling it — specific section names, specific gaps. The graded finding is whether the template REQUIRES each element or merely permits it, and specifically whether it requires 'what could not be established and why', which most omit. Credit a learner who discovered their template has no place for a witness who was not interviewed, or for evidence sought and not obtained. A confident audit with no specifics reads as memory and should be pushed on.

dimensions.name: The rebuild marks rungs, section by section
dimensions.criteria: The elements structure implemented, with each section marked for the rung it contains so a future user can see where AI is permitted. Elements one to four are rungs one and two; five and six are rungs four and five. Credit a narrative summary retained and explicitly labelled as a summary of the elements rather than as the findings — that is the compromise the module invites and adopting it deliberately scores well. Credit template language that would stop a user putting a finding in a factual section.

dimensions.name: The mapping check is a mechanism, not an intention
dimensions.criteria: Concrete: how allegations become a numbered list at intake, when the mapping runs, what its output looks like, who reads it. Must include the explicit statement that 'outside scope' and 'insufficient evidence to determine' are resolutions while silence is not. Two things earn top marks: running the check against the COMPLAINANT'S OWN FRAMING rather than the investigator's restatement, and a written prompt if the check is AI-assisted. 'We will check that all allegations are addressed' is an intention and should be named as one.

dimensions.name: The rung discipline holds in the learner's own language
dimensions.criteria: Two tests. First, do the prohibited-pattern lines name the real patterns — evaluative adjectives in factual sections, state-of-mind verbs, unattributed passives? Second, and more important, does the learner's own register-audit instruction stay inside the line? Penalize and name directly any instruction asking a model to rewrite neutrally, assess whether a conclusion is supported, or judge plausibility — those are the module's central error appearing in the learner's own template. The correct shape asks a model to identify and QUOTE sentences containing characterizations or conclusions, leaving the fix to a human.

dimensions.name: Provenance and the privilege question were addressed
dimensions.criteria: What the template records about how the document was produced: contemporaneous notes kept separately, the chronology preserved, AI involvement recorded as a line in the file rather than as a disclaimer on the report. Then the privilege sentence — is the matter type ever conducted under privilege, and has anybody asked counsel about AI use in it. The learner is NOT graded on legal accuracy here: 'no, and I will ask this month' is complete and full credit. Credit recognizing that if a matter may be privileged the AI question belongs in the engagement rather than afterwards.

dimensions.name: The delta and the position
dimensions.criteria: Predicted element count against actual, with an account of the gap — an over-prediction is the common and intended finding, since templates permit more than they require. Accuracy is never graded. Plus a committed position on the module's claim engaging the real counter-argument: that an elements report is unreadable by the people who must act, that some findings are genuinely narrative findings, and that a floor becomes a ceiling for good investigators. The position MUST answer whether elements are a floor or a form, whether they would accept a well-argued narrative report, and if so WHAT THEY WOULD CHECK INSTEAD for the unaddressed allegation. A learner who reaches for the mapping check as the structure-independent mechanism has understood the argument and should score at the top.
